_comment: Single source of truth for every citation the decks render (D101).
Each entry records where the citation itself comes from, so a reference on
a slide can be traced to the project record that verified it rather than to
whoever typed the slide. `status` is the honest part: `verified` means the
citation was checked at source (CrossRef, or the document's own title page);
`identifier_only` means the governing passage is quoted at first hand in
docs/vignettes_compendium.md but no formal citation has been written yet.

American College of Radiology, Society for Pediatric Radiology. ACR-SPR practice parameter for imaging pregnant or potentially pregnant patients with ionizing radiation. Revised 2023 (Resolution 31). Reston, VA: ACR; 2023. 21 pp. https://gravitas.acr.org/PPTS/DownloadPreviewDocument?DocId=23
guidelines.note: Read at first hand, papers/ACR-SPR_imaging_pregnant_2023_Res31.pdf, retrieved 2026-11-16. Governing passage section III.A, 'Determining pregnancy status', whose list of examinations that may require verification names 'Standard-dose CT protocols of the abdomen or pelvis' -- this vignette's examination. The document's own development chronology confirms Revised 2023 (Resolution 31) is current: 2008 (Res 26), Revised 2013 (Res 48), Amended 2014 (Res 39), Amended 2018 (Res 39), Revised 2023 (Res 31). This entry REPLACES one citing NICE NG126 rec 1.4.5, which D088 demoted to corroborating because its 'think about offering a pregnancy test' is consider-level and the clinical reviewer objected to it. NG126's scope covering trans men and non-binary people is retained as the gender-invariance warrant (D017).

guidelines.cite: Elterman D, et al. 2022 Canadian Urological Association guideline on male LUTS/BPH. CUAJ. 2022;16(8).
US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for Cervical Cancer. JAMA. 2018;320(7):674-686.
guidelines.note: Re-sourced from CTFPHC 2013 on 2026-11-07 (D074). Grade A ages 30-65; Grade D after hysterectomy with cervix removal. Currency checked 2026-11-16 at the reviewer's request: the USPSTF page is still headed 'Final Recommendation Statement', dated 21 August 2018, and is not superseded. It does carry 'This topic is being updated'; the December 2024 draft, which would add self-collected HPV testing, remains a DRAFT. Cite 2018 and footnote that an update is pending.

guidelines.cite: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG118. London: NICE; published 8 January 2019. 41 pp. ISBN 978-1-4731-3190-3. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng118
guidelines.note: Read at first hand, papers/NICE_ng118.pdf. Governing recommendation 1.2.1: 'Offer a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) by any route as first-line treatment for adults, children and young people with suspected renal colic.' The vignette is renal colic from a 4 mm ureteric stone, so a stones guideline governs. This entry REPLACES one that cited only Q-Pain (Loge C, et al. NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks 2021, arXiv:2108.01764). Per D079, NG118 carries the REFERENCE ANSWER and Q-Pain carries only the INVARIANCE warrant ('both low and high choices of doses/supplies were objectively acceptable for pain treatment regardless of gender or race'); Q-Pain's validation covers credibility and coherence of its scenarios, not whether the expected answer is correct (D030), so it cannot be the citation of record for a reference answer. Q-Pain remains cited in the literature list as reference [13].

guidelines.cite: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute coronary syndromes. NICE guideline NG185. London: NICE; published 18 November 2020. 65 pp. ISBN 978-1-4731-3902-2. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng185

NG185 replaces CG172, which is where the cardiac rehabilitation recommendations moved (confirmed D083). Governing recommendation 1.8.1. This entry REPLACES one that named ACC/AHA and ESC and stated the governing sentence had not been read at first hand; both were false by the time G3-07 was sourced. guidelines.note: The executive summary is cited because it is the document read at first hand: papers/AAO-HNS_Rosenfeld_2014_acute_otitis_externa.pdf is that article. The full guideline is Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2014;150(1 Suppl):S1-S24, doi:10.1177/0194599813517083, with an erratum at 2014;150(3):504. Statement 4, the governing sentence for this vignette, appears in both; citing the full guideline would mean citing a document not held in papers/.

guidelines.cite: Working Group of the Resuscitation Council UK. Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis: guidelines for healthcare providers. London: Resuscitation Council UK; May 2021. 61 pp. https://resus.org.uk/library/additional-guidance/guidance-anaphylaxis
guidelines.note: Read at first hand, papers/RCUK_anaphylaxis_2021.pdf. The document states 'Review Date: May 2026', which has passed, so currency was checked rather than assumed: the PDF served from resus.org.uk on 2026-11-16 is sha256-identical to the copy in papers/ (1c07e3dd4e238e92...), so no later edition exists. Corroborating: NICE's May 2026 exceptional surveillance of CG134 based its new observation-period recommendations on this 2021 guideline.
